# Portals: 7-Day Women's Ayahuasca Retreat near Tulum, Mexico

> Portals is a women-only, seven-day Ayahuasca retreat held in a secluded jungle sanctuary near Tulum, Quintana Roo, Mexico, run by experienced facilitators who have led 400+ ceremonies since 2022. The next retreat runs January 15–21, 2027. Website: https://portals.theheartbased.co/

Portals is not a medical or therapeutic service. It does not diagnose, treat or promise to cure any condition. 

## About

Portals is a women-only, seven-day Ayahuasca retreat hosted near Tulum, Mexico. It offers a safe space with experienced facilitators who have led over 400 ceremonies. The retreat is designed as a full journey, not a single ceremony, for women ready to release the old and bring in the new. The program integrates ceremonial plant medicine with sound healing, movement (ecstatic dance, yoga), art, vocal activation, local traditions, and structured rest to support reflection and personal growth, with an emphasis on small-group care, modern comfort in nature, safety protocols, guided preparation and integraiton.

The intention behind the retreat is to bring women together, to activate each other's potential, and to help each participant step into the version of herself she wants to become: to move through stagnation and feel supported through whatever she's experiencing, whether that's a life transition, a career transition, divorce, or becoming an empty nester.

## Who this retreat is for

- Women who feel they're ready to expand, or sense there's more to their potential than what they're currently living, not necessarily unhappy, just ready for a next chapter.
- Women who habitually put everyone else's needs first because they're naturally caring, big-hearted people.
- Healers (reiki practitioners, sound healers), holistic coaches, studio owners, nutritionists, and others already immersed in holistic health, alternative healing, and sound work.
- Professionals, social workers, remote workers, and established entrepreneurs moving through a transition, feeling a pull to expand, or wanting to reconnect with themselves and meet like-minded women.
- Women traveling or planning to travel to Mexico who want an immersive, authentic experience.
- Women curious about sitting with Ayahuasca for the first time (or returning to it) who want to do so safely, in nature, with modern comfort, in a small group, with experienced facilitators.
- High-performing, high-achieving woman

## The program

One Ayahuasca ceremony anchors a full week designed around integration, not just the ceremony itself:

- 1 Ayahuasca ceremony held with experienced facilitators and live medicine music.
- Sound bath sessions for nervous system regulation and cleansing.
- Guided somatic integration for grounding.
- An intentional silent morning after the ceremony, for individual reflection and inward focus.
- Temazcal and flower bath rituals rooted in local Mexican tradition.
- Gentle yoga supporting mobility, breath, nervous system reset, and body awareness.
- A vocal activation workshop exploring voice, expression, confidence, and inner power.
- Ecstatic dance paired with a cacao ceremony, for movement-based release and opening the heart.
- Shamanic art-making for processing and creative activation.
- Sharing circles and music jams for peer reflection and connection.
- A cenote swim and time in nature within the Mayan jungle setting.
- 1 pre-retreat preparation call covering expectations, packing, and intention-setting.
- 1 post-retreat integration call to support applying insights and habit change at home.
- Nutritious meals throughout, with vegan, gluten-free, and dairy-free options, plus an on-site snack and tea bar available at all times.
- A personal photoshoot to document the milestone and mark the new chapter.
- Lodging in a luxury jungle sanctuary, with private and shared room options.
- Direct access to hosts Shannon and Debbie for questions, before and during the retreat.

## Why Portals

- Women-only cohort: gender-specific space and psychological safety.
- Intentionally intimate group size, for personalized attention and deeper bonds between participants.
- Facilitation team with extensive ceremony experience: 400+ ceremonies led collectively, running retreats since 2022.
- Multiple healing modalities in one program: sound healing, somatic and movement work, art and creativity, music, Temazcal, and one Ayahuasca ceremony, not plant medicine alone.
- Designed as a full journey, not just a ceremony: the program is built to help participants bring insights into daily life eveb after the retreat, not only sit with the medicine.
- Guided preparation and aftercare built into the program (a preparation call, a preparation checklist, and a post-retreat integration call) for peace of mind before and after.
- A secluded jungle location with the comfort of a modern sanctuary: nature immersion without sacrificing comfort.
- A personal photoshoot included as a bonus gift, to help each woman mark her chapter.
- Responsive hosts: Shannon and Debbie are directly reachable with questions.

## Values

- Every retreat is held with integrity, respect, and care.
- Gratitude is given to the land, and to the guides and spirits that hold the container.
- The intention is for every woman to step into the best version of herself, to feel and see how special she is, to break old patterns, and to know she is loved.
- Every soul who comes is honored.

## Pricing

- From 2,350 USD per person (early-bird), reduced from 2,650 USD.
- Room options: The Serenity Suite (private room, private bathroom); The Hearts Haven (shared with 1 woman, own bed, shared bathroom); The Trinity (shared with 2 women, own bed, shared bathroom).
- All room options include the full retreat program and meals.
- Flexible payment options are available.
- Joining the waitlist gives early-bird pricing, the full brochure, and first choice of room.

## Safety and suitability

- Every participant completes a safety assessment before joining.
- Medication contraindications are reviewed together.
- Conditions that are not generally recommended include: antidepressants (such as SSRIs or MAOIs) or antipsychotic medications; psychiatric conditions or family histories of certain mental health disorders; surgery within the past three months; heart conditions; uncontrolled high blood pressure; uncontrolled diabetes; epilepsy; active addiction; pregnancy.
- If any of these apply, participation may still be possible; it is assessed case by case.
- First-time participants are common and welcome. A preparation guide is provided.
- No participant is pressured into any activity. Group agreements are set so everyone feels supported.
